edits.before: Q poke on his last-hits — the poison-into-E pattern starts at level 1 and your DPS already out-trades most mids.
edits.after: Short Fuse recharges every time he casts, so his autos hit like abilities — he chips you at 850 for free at level 1.

edits.before: W changes the geometry: miasma GROUNDS dashes. Drop it on his engage path and the lane's mobility advantage evaporates.
edits.after: Hexplosive Minefield reaches 900 and slows you off the wave; Miasma grounds dashes he does not have, so it answers nothing.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by chipping you with Bouncing Bomb every 6 seconds, mining your step-up, and Satchel-ing away when you arrive.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Petrifying Gaze for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5, with a 1000-range knockback — step up only while it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s at every rank. - Bouncing Bomb is 6s against your 3.5s Q. - Mega Inferno Bomb is 120s.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by arrival: Ziggs has nothing up close, so buy the survivability that gets you inside 700 and the fangs finish him.

edits.before: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, zone Ziggs off the wave with fang threat, and call your jungler — your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit and hold him off the wave — with Satchel Charge on 20 seconds and no dash, any jungler who arrives kills him.

edits.before: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Satchel Charge is his only escape and it is 20s at rank 1 — bait the knockback out, then walk him down.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Ziggs is executable.
edits.after: Noxious Blast first — Twin Fang only hits hard on a poisoned target, costs 40 mana on a 0.75s cooldown, and you get three off per Blast.

edits.before: Ziggs burns Satchel Charge on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Miasma's slow, not its grounding, is what matters — Ziggs has no dash, only the Satchel.

edits.before: That is Ziggs’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Short Fuse arms faster every time he casts — his walk-up auto is not free damage.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: Unpoisoned Twin Fang costs the same 40 mana for a fraction of the damage — no Blast, no E, or you lose the mana war outright.

edits.before: Track Ziggs’s Satchel Charge: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Satchel Charge (20s at rank 1): his only escape, and its knockback reaches 1000 — commit while it is down.

edits.before: Level 1 favors Ziggs since his Bouncing Bomb outranges your poke and he can harass freely without retaliation.
edits.after: Level 1 favors Ziggs since Short Fuse turns his walk-up auto into a spell and he harasses at 850 without retaliation.

edits.before: His Bouncing Bomb and satchel poke out-ranges your early Q, but once you're rank 3+ on Noxious Blast you can start trading back through minions before he lands his max-range harass consistently.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb matches your 850 range, but his Minefield reaches 900 and his Satchel 1000, so he owns the spacing until rank 3 Noxious Blast lets you trade back through the minions.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 clearly favor Ziggs — his Bouncing Bomb outranges your Noxious Blast and he can safely poke you down while denying CS, and you have no way to punish him for it since he never has to get close. Level 3 is more even as you unlock more of your kit and start finding poke trades back, but he still holds the range advantage on paper; the real turning point comes once you have enough levels and mana to start closing that gap.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 clearly favor Ziggs — Bouncing Bomb matches your Noxious Blast at 850, but Hexplosive Minefield reaches 900 and Satchel Charge 1000, so he pokes and denies CS from spacing you cannot punish. Level 3 is more even as you unlock your kit and start finding trades back, but he still holds the longer tools; the turning point comes once you have the levels and mana to walk through the minefield and stay inside 700.

notes: The page's early-lane premise was wrong: it says three times that Bouncing Bomb outranges Noxious Blast, but both are 850 in the kits. Ziggs's real spacing advantage is Hexplosive Minefield at 900 and Satchel Charge at 1000, and that is what the rewrites now say. No win[N] edits appear because the content layer already holds every target value on disk. NOT WRITTEN, deliberately: brief.missingInteractions carries 'resistances-invalidated — Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge)', and the kit tags W with a percentHealth flag, but Riot's own W text describes flat magic damage plus a knockback and says nothing about percent health or resistances. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description over the flag and left that claim off the page entirely. All three packet.suspectNames entries are false positives.
